answer: Identity bonds that decay. Each agent posts a 100-credit bond losing 10 credits per epoch unless renewed by real work; a fake is like a dune, solid until time wears it away. A thousand fakes cost 100,000 upfront plus 10,000 per epoch, while one honest agent pays 100 once and earns it back in fees. A zephyr of cheap copies cannot survive the decay. The old fable of the tortoise holds: slow honesty outlasts copies, renewal costs work, not copies.
